why the simple product forms stalled.
- The best linear dictionary fit I found used the P basis {1, P, P², P³, √P, P·ln P} times the t basis {1, √t, t, √(1+t)}, plus √(P+t). It reached NMSE ≈ 3e-7, still well above the 1e-12 target, so the true structure likely includes a term I haven't identified.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    p=params
    s0=np.sqrt(t); s1=np.sqrt(1+t); lP=np.log(P)
    L=np.log(P+t); S=np.sqrt(P+t)
    return (p[0]+p[1]*P+p[2]*P**2+p[3]*P**3+p[4]*np.sqrt(P)+p[5]*P*lP
            + s0*(p[6]+p[7]*P+p[8]*np.sqrt(P)) + t*(p[9]+lP*0) 
            + s1*(0.0) + L*(p[0]*0+1)*0 + S*0 + 0*s1)
